guideline_text:
Scope: image annotation labels, bounding boxes and polygons. These are team-authored development guidelines for extraction verification.
Definitions: a person is a real human in the scene, excluding people on posters or screens; a car is a passenger motor vehicle, excluding buses and trucks.
Uncertainty policy: when blur, darkness, occlusion or small image size prevents a reliable judgement, report uncertain for human review.
1. Allowed annotation labels are person and car.
2. Each annotation label must name the actual object visible inside its geometry; a visible person must not be labelled car.
3. Each supplied bounding box must lie entirely within the image bounds.
4. A fully visible person's bounding box must include the whole visible head, including hair and headwear.
5. A fully visible person's bounding box must include the visible lower legs and feet, including footwear.
6. A person's bounding box must include every other visible body part, including raised arms, hands and elbows.
7. For a person partly hidden by another object or the image edge, annotate only visible portions and do not extend boxes or polygons over body parts that cannot be seen.
8. A person polygon must follow that person's visible boundary without being displaced into the background or enclosing large regions of background.
9. Every polygon part in one person annotation must belong to that same person and must not outline a different person or object.
10. For this development test, a person's bounding box must be at least 20 pixels high, measured in original image coordinates.
